## Strategy
Use accepted computation dependency `162283c7d25bcc9b6cf77717e180ce1c85e4bdcbe2d0dbabc186aab75e18d126` (exit \(0\); script SHA-256 `16fd86d80765622e58e1da6f79707ddf13a2f664cccea1c42a38e798b9d07680`; output SHA-256 `818902094d31864cfaca06b0649fb4fc447ab0cc889c87f4d3a885dd54996e93`). Its explicit inputs are the \(c=6\) interval, degrees \(4,\ldots,32\), and \(h\)-degrees \(1,\ldots,4\).

Its quotient ranks are \(1,1,2,1,1\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8\), and \(0\) thereafter; torsion is absent. Thus
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6.
\]
With accepted generation of each six-element family and the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion, each induces a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\), hence a basis map. Therefore neither family has a proper generating subfamily. The requested \(i=j=p=2,c=6\) minimality corollary is established relative to these accepted dependencies.
